content: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), commonly referred to as blood clots, encompasses two serious conditions: deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). It is essential to understand the symptoms, risk factors, and treatment options for these conditions to ensure timely diagnosis and management. Testing and Diagnosis for Venous Thromboembolism Blood clots are diagnosed through a combination of clinical evaluation and diagnostic testing. Healthcare providers may use imaging studies such as ultrasound for DVT or CT pulmonary angiography for PE. Blood tests, including D-dimer assays, can also assist in identifying the presence of a clot. Treatment options vary depending on the severity and location of the clot but often include anticoagulant medications to prevent further clot formation and, in some cases, thrombolytic therapy to dissolve existing clots. Risk Factors for Blood Clots Certain factors increase the likelihood of developing blood clots. These include prolonged immobility (e.g., during long flights or hospital stays), recent surgery, trauma, cancer, pregnancy, use of hormonal contraceptives, and genetic predispositions such as thrombophilia. Understanding these risk factors is critical for prevention and early intervention. Stop the Clot®—What Every Healthcare Professional Should Know E-Learning Course Healthcare professionals can enhance their knowledge of VTE by participating in the Stop the Clot® e-learning course. This program provides detailed guidance on identifying, treating, and managing patients with blood clots, ensuring evidence-based care and improved patient outcomes. Materials and Multimedia About Blood Clots A variety of educational resources are available to help individuals and healthcare providers learn more about blood clots. These materials include brochures, videos, and infographics designed to raise awareness and promote prevention strategies. Stop the Clot, Spread the Word® Campaign Resources The Stop the Clot, Spread the Word® campaign offers shareable resources aimed at educating the public about the risks, symptoms, and prevention of blood clots. These materials are designed to empower individuals to recognize warning signs and seek medical attention promptly. Real Stories from People Who Have Experienced Blood Clots Personal accounts from individuals who have experienced blood clots provide valuable insights into the impact of these conditions. These stories highlight the importance of early detection, proper treatment, and ongoing management to prevent complications and improve quality of life.
